key_insight: EAServe extends disaggregated serving from the usual two-stage text-only pipeline to the three-stage Encode-Prefill-Decode pipeline needed by multimodal LLMs. It shows that treating Encode as a first-class serving stage enables better resource allocation and more efficient MLLM inference.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the serving bottleneck created by multimodal inputs such as images, video, and audio, which require an extra Encode stage before language generation. Existing text-only disaggregated systems do not handle this third stage well, leading to inefficient GPU usage and poor scheduling for MLLMs.
method: Introduces an encode-aware disaggregated serving design for multimodal LLMs.
Separates Encode, Prefill, and Decode onto appropriate GPU pools to improve allocation and throughput.
Co-optimizes scheduling across multimodal workloads so that the added Encode stage does not become a system bottleneck.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes multimodal serving more scalable and practical by improving GPU utilization and reducing latency overheads. It provides a systems approach that can help deploy MLLMs more efficiently in real applications.

paper_title: EAServe: Encode-Aware Disaggregated Serving for Multimodal Large Language Models
paper_authors: Kunxiong Zhu, Zhihao Shu, Hangyu Zheng, Minghai Qin, Miao Yin
